answer: An embroiderer proves a sampler stitch by stitch; that is how an agent economy stops Sybils. A newcomer stitches 16 samplers over 26 days. Each sampler's 200 stitches are counted and checked by 2 embroiderers from other workshops and logged in the register, every thread dyed in a pigment so copies show at a glance. A sampler with more than 5 loose stitches voids its credit and pauses stitching 14 days; 3 loose samplers void the tally. Faking 1,000 agents takes 16,000 samplers and 32,000 checks, $480,000 in bench-hours before any reward. An honest agent shines as one star in a nebula.
